answer: Every claim climbs the jetty of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the terrace re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, unlocked only after continuous uptime, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. The signal of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a cause and effect, two sentences register, it stays short.
